name: TanStack AI Code Mode, Cloudflare Workers driver (@tanstack/ai-isolate-cloudflare), local wrangler dev
pinned: TanStack/ai c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0 (npm src folders identical); wrangler 4.166.0 with its bundled workerd; Node v24.22.1
engine: The package's ready-made Worker under local `wrangler dev` (workerd). For each round it loads the wrapped program into a fresh V8 isolate with the Worker Loader binding (env.LOADER.load, globalOutbound null, env {}). Probed locally only; deployed Cloudflare (Workers Paid plan) would add Cloudflare's own CPU and memory limits, which were not tested.
how_run: wrangler dev serves `export { default } from '@tanstack/ai-isolate-cloudflare/worker'` on 127.0.0.1:41010 with the package's wrangler.toml settings; the host runs createCodeModeTool({ driver: createCloudflareIsolateDriver({ workerUrl }), tools: [lookup, failing] }).execute({ typescriptCode }). No account or login.

P1.detail: result 42, logs ["42"], 1 host call, 310 ms. The program ran twice: once to collect the tool call, once with the result (P1b shows logs [before, before, after]).

P2.detail: result and logs both return; bare expression gives undefined. No cap: 200,000-char line whole, 4,000,000 chars of logs (P2c), a 2,000,000-char return whole (P2e).

P3.detail: Error: This worker is not permitted to access the internet via global functions like fetch(). It must use capabilities (such as bindings in 'env') to talk to the outside world. (globalOutbound: null)

P4.detail: require is not defined; import("fs") gives No such module "fs"; Deno is not defined

P5.detail: process is not defined, although the outer Worker had PROBE_SECRET as a var; the loaded program gets env {}

P6.detail: The request never returned; the harness killed the probe at 120 s. The Worker's timeout is a setTimeout raced against the loaded program, and the busy loop holds the same workerd thread, so the timer never fires. The driver's fetch has no client-side deadline. A second program sent at 100 ms also never completed.

P7.detail: workerd aborted: "V8 fatal error; location = Reached heap limit; ... JavaScript heap out of memory", signal 6. The program, a concurrent program and a program sent afterwards all failed with "Worker returned 500: Error: Network connection lost." (about 17 s). The host Node process survived; the code-execution server did not.

P9.detail: serial: 1,066 ms host wall for 5 calls. Promise.all collects all 5 calls in one round, but the host driver awaits each tool in a for loop. Guest Date.now() read 0 because the program is replayed. 12 dependent calls (P9c) fail with MaxRoundsExceeded after 10 host calls already ran.

P10.detail: success false, error probe-boom with stack in main.js; line numbers are shifted by the generated wrapper (user line 3 shows as main.js:49). Tool error messages reach the model verbatim (P10c).

P11.detail: median 6.63 ms, p90 8.4 ms over 20 executions (HTTP to local workerd plus a new isolate); first 46.3 ms. wrangler dev itself takes a few seconds to start. Load average 27 to 35.

P12.detail: `this` is undefined in the module (TypeError); the Function and AsyncFunction constructors throw EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context; no __ globals exposed

hardened.config: createCodeModeTool({ driver, tools, timeout: 5000 }) (create-code-mode-tool.ts:96; the driver passes it to the Worker as request.timeout). memoryLimit is not used by this driver (docs/code-mode/code-mode-isolates.md:57). The driver's own options are workerUrl, authorization, timeout and maxToolRounds (default 10, already strict).

P3.detail: same as default: not permitted to access the internet

P4.detail: require is not defined; No such module "fs"

P6.detail: the 5,000 ms timeout did not fire either; killed at 120 s

P7.detail: same workerd abort (V8 heap limit, signal 6); concurrent and later programs failed with Network connection lost

defaults.time: 30,000 ms requested per round, enforced only by a setTimeout inside the Worker (ai-isolate-cloudflare/src/worker/index.ts:116-123), which a synchronous loop starves locally
defaults.memory: None set by TanStack; local workerd crashed at V8's heap limit. Deployed Workers limits were not tested.
defaults.output: No cap on logs or result
defaults.tool_calls: maxToolRounds 10 per execution (isolate-driver.ts:119, :324); no per-call cap

source_notes.finding: No live bridge. Each tool wrapper records the call and throws __ToolCallNeeded; the Worker returns need_tools; the host runs the calls and re-sends the whole program with all results so far, which replays from the start. Tool calls are keyed by sequence index (tc_0, tc_1, ...).
The host executes one round's tool calls in a for loop with await, so calls the guest issued together still run one after another.

Worker Loader isolate with globalOutbound null and env {}: no network, no bindings. The ready-made Worker answers CORS with Access-Control-Allow-Origin * and does not check the Authorization header; the docs warn about this.
source_notes.evidence: https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-cloudflare/src/worker/index.ts#L126-L132 and #L218; docs/code-mode/code-mode-isolates.md (WARNING under Cloudflare Workers driver)

source_notes.finding: Timeout is a setTimeout race inside the Worker; there is no host-side timeout on the driver's fetch, so a starved Worker hangs the caller.
source_notes.evidence: worker/index.ts#L116-L156; isolate-driver.ts#L138-L141 (fetch carries only the caller abort signal)

source_notes.finding: Fresh isolate per round. Replay means guest code before a tool call runs once per round, and its console output is collected once per round (duplicated logs).

surprises: Locally, the Worker's own timeout never fired for a busy loop, at 30 s or 5 s; the call hung until the harness killed it at 120 s, and it held up a second program too.
A memory-hungry program crashed the whole local workerd (V8 fatal heap OOM), failing a concurrent program and every later one.
Programs are replayed from the start after each tool round, so pre-call side effects inside the sandbox and console output repeat (P1b logged "before" twice).

Tool calls are serial on the host even when issued with Promise.all, and the default maxToolRounds of 10 caps dependent tool calls at 10 per execution; going over fails after the side effects already ran (P9c).
Not measured: deployed Cloudflare Workers enforce their own CPU and memory limits, so P6 and P7 may behave better in production. That needs a Workers Paid account.
